newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi rises in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi rises in Beirut.

text.p: Two of the three bank shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange rose on Wednesday with Banque Audi jumping to $21 from $20 amid heavy demand.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $16.5 from $16.25 and Bank of Beirut was unchanged at $3.5625.
Brokers said demand for Banque Audi had been piling up for some time.

"The total value of traded Audi shares in the last 10 working days was a little bit more than $3.5 million, and today we had heavy demand so nobody could calm it down any more," Nabil Aoun, head of Fidus brokerage house, told Reuters.
Another reason for the rise was that Banque Audi's GDRs were rising on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange, he said.
"The Audi share is attractive, its GDR rose $1 to $24.75 within a week. So its rise is very rational compared with the other two listed banks on the BSE," Aoun said.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.16 percent to 139.66. The LISPI general index rose 0.36 percent to 84.4 and BLOM general index fell 1.03 percent to 915.4.
Solidere A shares fell to $10.25 from $10.5 and B shares were unchanged at $10.75.
Aoun said Wednesday was the first time in five days that demand for Solidere exceeded supply and this would be reflected later in the market.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
Total market turnover was 142,330 shares for a value of $1,355,603 compared with 171,744 shares for a value of $1,476,947 on Tuesday.
